title: content.shiftTiming
description: Moves a section of a content earlier or later by deltaSec, as dragging time-grid handles in OpenTune's time tool does: every handle whose output position lies in range moves by deltaSec and the other handles stay, so the audio next to the section is stretched or compressed. range is a closed interval: a handle exactly at its start and a handle exactly at its end both move (OpenTune selects the handles with start <= position <= end). So when two ranges of one batch share an end point, a handle at that point is moved twice, once by each range; adjacent ranges must not share an end point. range uses the content or the output clock; a content range is mapped through the grid at expectedGridRevision. Moves are limited as in OpenTune's time tool, in two passes, by the minimum spacing to the neighbouring handles; a limited move is applied as far as allowed and reported in clamped and with the warning CLAMPED (subject: the handle; data: {field: outputSec, requested, applied}). The time grid must have handles (content.editTimeGrid op seed), else NOT_READY(grid_not_seeded). If no handle lies in range, the call is a no-op. One call is one undo step. Rendering is queued again (sideEffects.reRenderQueued); exports wait for it (PROTOCOL.md section 19).
